newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prosecutor withdraws from scandal case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prosecutor withdraws from scandal case.

text.p: A Turkish prosecutor seeking to open the way for legal action against a government MP in a scandal over state-underworld links on Monday quit the case in disgust after his bid was rejected on technical grounds.

The state-run Anatolian news agency said prosecutor Nihat Artiran decided to withdraw from the case after the justice ministry last week rejected as incomplete his report calling for legal steps to lift deputy Mehmet Agar's parliamentary immunity.
"The ministry asked for the chief prosecutor to rewrite the report. This situation seems wrong to me and so I have decided to withdraw from the inquiry," Artiran told Anatolian.
Ankara's chief prosecutor Ilhan Mesutoglu will take over the case, the agency said.

The scandal broke on November 3 after an accident in which a wanted gangster, Abdullah Catli, and a leading policeman died in the same car. A government MP who heads an anti-guerrilla Kurdish militia was also in the car.

Agar, who quit as interior minister in November over the scandal, was accused last week of having signed a false police identity document for Catli, who was allegedly used by officials to kill Turkey's political opponents.

The media and opposition has alleged that leading officials directed hit squads to kill Kurdish rebel sympathisers and business rivals. More than 1,300 people have died since 1992 in unsolved political killings, human right activists say.
